title: Lior and the Oath
premise: Casper Eriksen, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent their whole life in the valley where magic cannot follow, guarding the secret of the gift and of Lior—the person they love most, whose soul was sold years ago to the court beneath the mountain to buy the valley's peace. When the crown declares a hunt for all gifted blood and soldiers breach the valley's wards, Casper flees with a hunted stranger named Vess, discovering that the hunt is a cover for harvesting souls to feed the mountain throne—and Lior's soul is the keystone keeping it alive. To steal Lior back, Casper must break their own oath, unbinding the words that give them power but also erase every memory of why they swore it. In the end, Casper chooses truth over loyalty: they shatter the oath, lose the gift and half their memories, but free Lior's soul and bring down the soul-fed crown, returning to a valley that can now be left.
about_author: Zephyrine Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath registers before turning to fiction. They write in a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where they claim the wind dictates the endings.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. We meet the valley where magic dies at the tree line, and Casper's quiet life tending goats and practicing sword-forms that hum with dormant power. A recurring dream of a voice calling from beneath stone hints at Lior. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness about to crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Wards
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Vess, a gifted fugitive bleeding ward-sickness, collapses at the valley's edge—impossible, since magic cannot cross. Casper hides her despite the law of silence. Emotional beat: first act of disloyalty to the oath, felt as physical pain.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Riders nail a royal proclamation to the valley gate: all gifted blood to be surrendered for 'the crown's protection.' Vess recognizes the seal—it belongs to the court beneath the mountain, where her own sister was taken. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Oath Costs
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Under interrogation by the village elder, Casper recites fragments of their oath and realizes each recitation has eaten memories—including everything about Lior except the name. Emotional beat: grief for stolen past; decision to leave the valley with Vess.

chapters.title: Crossing the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The moment they step beyond the wards, Casper's swordspeech ignites—words become cutting force—and the world floods with sensation they've never known. Soldiers tracking Vess attack; Casper kills for the first time. Emotional beat: intoxication and horror of power.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Traveling toward the mountain capital, Vess teaches Casper how the gifted survive the hunt: hiding, bribing, lying. Casper's honesty chafes against survival. They shelter with a family who betrays them for reward money. Emotional beat: trust tested, then hardened.

chapters.title: The Soul Market
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the city of Greyhollow, souls are traded openly as 'vessels.' Casper finds a broker holding a ledger of the crown's purchases—and Lior's name, dated the year of the valley's founding treaty. Emotional beat: hope and fury entwined.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The broker offers information in exchange for a piece of Vess's own soul. She pays. What she learns: Lior's soul isn't stored—it powers the throne itself, and the hunt exists to find replacements. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the sickening scale of the conspiracy.

chapters.title: Words Like Knives
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Ambushed by a hunt-captain who is also an oath-bound speaker—one of the old order Casper thought extinct. Their duel is fought entirely in spoken force. Casper wins but learns the order serves the throne willingly. Emotional beat: disillusionment with legacy.

chapters.title: The Memory Beneath the Scar
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Wounded, feverish, Casper dreams fully into the erased night of the oath-swearing: they gave up Lior themselves, believing it would save the valley. Emotional beat: self-betrayal revealed; guilt becomes the engine of the quest.

chapters.title: Confession at the Wayshrine
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Casper confesses everything to Vess at a ruined shrine. Instead of condemnation, Vess reveals she sold her sister's location to save herself once. Two betrayers make a pact: truth between them, always. Emotional beat: fragile absolution.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The hunt-captain returns with reinforcements; Greyhollow burns around them. Casper uses swordspeech publicly for the first time, exposing themselves to save strangers—becoming exactly what the proclamation hunts. Emotional beat: loyalty to others over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Guided by the broker's map, they descend through abandoned mine-shafts into the court's under-halls, where the walls are veined with imprisoned light—harvested souls. Emotional beat: awe curdling into revulsion.

chapters.title: The Court of Kept Voices
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Disguised as tribute-bearers, they witness the throne: a lattice of souls murmuring prophecies to the crown. Among the voices, Casper hears Lior's cadence. Emotional beat: longing made unbearable and immediate.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Brought before the sovereign, Casper is offered a place in the restored order of speakers—if they surrender Vess. The crown shows them Lior's soul, still aware, still waiting. Emotional beat: the ultimate temptation; loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Casper refuses; the court turns on them both. Vess springs the escape plan, sacrificing her remaining soul-fragment to shatter a ward-lattice. Prisoned light spills through the halls like released birds. Emotional beat: reckless, blazing hope.

chapters.title: Lior
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Reaching the throne's heart, Casper finally speaks to Lior's soul—a conversation across the boundary of flesh, learning what Lior has endured and forgiven. But freeing the keystone will collapse the mountain. Emotional beat: reunion and impossible choice.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. To unbind Lior, Casper must unbind themselves—renouncing the oath aloud, knowing it will erase the memories that remain and strip their power. They speak the renunciation with Lior's voice steadying theirs. Emotional beat: surrender as the truest act of love.

chapters.title: The Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The throne gutters out; the court's servants flee or fall silent as their harvested purpose dies. The mountain begins to collapse. Vess drags a hollow-eyed, memory-stripped Casper toward the daylight shafts. Emotional beat: desperate tenderness amid ruin.

chapters.title: What Survives the Dark
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Half-conscious, Casper experiences memory returning in fragments—not the oath, but Lior: a laugh, a promise, a face. Power gone, identity remade around love instead of duty. Emotional beat: rebirth through loss.

chapters.title: The Valley That Can Be Left
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. They return to find the valley's wards dead with the throne that fed them. Villagers are free to go—or stay by choice. Vess departs to search for her sister's scattered soul-light. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting, gratitude.

chapters.title: Oath Unspoken
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Standing at the tree line with Lior's freed soul finding its way home, Casper plants their sword in the earth and walks past it without looking back. No oath binds them now; they choose each day anyway. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—an ending defined by freedom rather than victory.
